notice: Project-authored condensed descriptors for every source dimension and score point. Not a verbatim official rubric or validated scoring instrument.

ideas_content.6: Precise central ideas; insightful balanced development with significant credible support; thoroughly develop claims/counterclaims when argumentative.
ideas_content.5: Clear central ideas with carefully selected support and balanced explanation; develop claims/counterclaims when argumentative.
ideas_content.4: Clear purpose with relevant specific support; acknowledge/address counterclaims when argumentative.
ideas_content.3: Ambiguous or obvious ideas, general support; argumentative counterclaims ignored or mishandled.
ideas_content.2: Unclear purpose and vague, insufficient, irrelevant or repetitive detail.
ideas_content.1: No central idea or meaningful development.

organization.6: Compelling structure and smooth sequencing; varied transitions, engaging opening and satisfying conclusion.
organization.5: Strong structure and effective sequence, transitions and boundaries.
organization.4: Clear coherent order and paragraphs, possibly formulaic; adequate links and boundaries.
organization.3: Inconsistent or rigid organization; weak boundaries and repetitive links.
organization.2: Hard-to-follow sequence; misplaced details and missing or weak boundaries.
organization.1: Disjointed order without useful links or identifiable structure.

voice.6: Purposeful formal, objective voice fits disciplinary norms and strongly engages the intended audience.
voice.5: Consistent formal, objective voice fits topic and discipline with clear audience awareness.
voice.4: Generally appropriate formal style and objective tone; some inconsistent distance from the audience.
voice.3: Uneven formality, tone and audience awareness; the voice is inconsistent.
voice.2: Little audience awareness; flat or overly personal tone does not fit disciplinary expectations.
voice.1: No effective audience connection or appropriate voice; style and tone undermine communication.

word_choice.6: Exceptionally precise, varied and purposeful vocabulary; vivid or discipline-specific language strengthens meaning.
word_choice.5: Precise varied vocabulary and effective imagery or terminology.
word_choice.4: Clear functional vocabulary with enough variety to avoid repetition.
word_choice.3: Generic or repetitive language, occasional misuse and strained expression.
word_choice.2: Monotonous, vague or misused words weaken meaning.
word_choice.1: Extremely limited or misused vocabulary obscures meaning.

sentence_fluency.6: Skillful rhythm and varied syntax emphasize meaning; strong control including purposeful fragments when appropriate.
sentence_fluency.5: Smooth rhythm and carefully varied, well-controlled sentences.
sentence_fluency.4: Generally fluid reading with some variety; strong simple-sentence control.
sentence_fluency.3: Mechanical or repetitive sentences with awkward passages and limited complex-sentence control.
sentence_fluency.2: Choppy or rambling sentences impede reading; little syntactic variety.
sentence_fluency.1: Incomplete or disjointed sentences and confusing syntax obscure meaning.

conventions.6: Exceptional control across a wide range; very rare minor errors, little editing needed.
conventions.5: Strong control and effective punctuation; few minor errors.
conventions.4: Generally correct conventions; minor errors preserve readability and meaning.
conventions.3: Limited control; errors begin to distract or hinder reading.
conventions.2: Frequent substantial errors impair readability and require major editing.
conventions.1: Pervasive severe errors obstruct meaning and require extensive editing.

use_of_sources.6: Synthesize/analyze multiple authoritative sources; integrate original paraphrases, accurate quotations, complete citations and bibliography.
use_of_sources.5: Use multiple authoritative sources with smooth attribution, accurate quotations and complete documentation.
use_of_sources.4: Use several authoritative sources, acknowledge limitations, paraphrase independently and generally document correctly.
use_of_sources.3: Limited or unreliable sources, patchy attribution, overly close paraphrasing or incomplete bibliography.
use_of_sources.2: Misrepresented ideas, near-copying, missing/wrong citations or substantially defective bibliography.
use_of_sources.1: Little source use or undocumented copying; absent citations and bibliography.

scope_notes: High-school guide shared across grades 9–12, not a separate grade-12 rubric.
Assess only textual evidence; do not infer student motivation, actual research process or unprovided source reliability.
This application uses the source-based task variant and requires supplied sources to assess Use of Sources.
Informative writing does not require counterclaims; an objective explanatory/argumentative tone replaces narrative intimacy.
total_policy: Display-only unweighted sum; no cross-provider score conversion or proficiency decision.
not_scorable_policy: Project abstention only when evidence cannot support scoring; the Oregon guide provides 1–6 anchors, not this NS category. Weak writing normally earns a source-scale score rather than abstention.
